verdict.rationale: Logseq's own Publishing feature lets users select individual pages with `publish:: true` (no pages are public by default) and publishes the graph as a single-page web app with custom CSS/JS, and one community user praises the publishing features. However, the evidence does not show that links between published pages keep working, that publishing and hosting happen entirely in-app, or any hands-on test of the result. missing for 10: explicit evidence that inter-note links resolve on the published site, documentation of an in-app publish-to-host workflow without external hosting steps, independent hands-on corroboration of a browsable digital garden.

support.subject: As a researcher, I can publish selected notes as a browsable website — a digital garden with working links — without leaving the app

citations.quote: By default no pages are public. Individual pages can be marked as public with the property `publish:: true`.
This feature publishes a graph as a [[Publish Web]], single page application (SPA).
Published apps can read user configuration from [[config.edn]], [[custom.css]], [[custom.js]] and [[export.css]].
Appreciates the publishing features and GitHub sync
